title: Eat, My Coat, Eat
text:
Nasreddin Hodja was invited to a wedding feast. He came straight from working in his fields, dressed in his old, patched and dusty clothes.

Nobody paid any attention to him. The servants seated him at the far end, the host did not greet him, and the dishes of rice and meat passed by without reaching him. After a while Nasreddin got up quietly and slipped out.

He hurried home, washed, and put on his finest fur coat and a fresh turban. Then he walked back to the feast. This time the host rushed to welcome him at the door, led him to the place of honor, and pressed the best food upon him.

Nasreddin took the sleeve of his splendid coat and dipped it into the soup. "Eat, my coat, eat," he said, pushing it toward the plates. The other guests stared at him. The host asked what on earth he was doing.

"When I came in my old clothes, nobody offered me a thing," said Nasreddin. "Now I am wearing this coat, and everything is given to it. So it seems only right that the coat should eat."
lesson: Notice whether you treat people according to their clothes, title or status. The person is the same whatever they wear, and so should your respect be.
people: Nasreddin Hodja, a host and guests
source: Nasreddin Hodja tales (Turkish and wider Middle Eastern folk tradition)
caveat: Nasreddin is a folk figure, and the stories attached to him were collected over centuries.
